title: Redwood POC scoping with Bayfront Health - security pilot
summary: POC scoping call focused on security and compliance requirements for a pilot: SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and on-prem/VPC considerations. Discussed success criteria (latency/throughput targets, data residency), workload sizing for peak business hours, benchmark plan, timeline (4-8 week pilot), and next steps to share security pack and schedule an on-site architecture review.
action_items: Jordan Kim - Share SOC 2 and ISO attestation docs + security pack by 2029-05-24
Priya Rao - Draft benchmark plan and spreadsheet (latency/throughput, sample prompts) by 2029-05-27
Marcus Lee - Provide representative traffic profile and dataset samples by 2029-05-25
Dr. Aaron Patel - Confirm minimum encryption/HSM requirements and KMS provider by 2029-05-29
Samir Gupta - Schedule architecture review with Bayfront infra team week of 2029-05-28
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack (SOC 2/ISO reports, pen test summary) and SSO integration guide
Customer to share traffic profile and list of stakeholders for pilot
Schedule 90-minute technical architecture review (on-prem/VPC) with Bayfront infra and security
Agree on benchmark metrics and run 2-day performance run during pilot week 3
transcript:
Meeting header: 2029-05-22 15:00 PDT | Duration: 55 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Kim, Priya Rao, Samir Gupta (Redwood) — Lena Morales, Dr. Aaron Patel, Marcus Lee, Zoe Han, Ethan Brooks (Bayfront)

[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood. Quick intros around the room?
[00:08] Lena Morales: Hi, I'm Lena, VP Eng at Bayfront, I'll be owning the program internally.
[00:12] Dr. Aaron Patel: Aaron, CISO. I'll be leading the security review.
[00:16] Marcus Lee: Marcus, Platform Lead, I'll coordinate infra and benchmarks.
[00:20] Zoe Han: Zoe, privacy.
[00:22] Ethan Brooks: Ethan, DevOps.
[00:25] Priya Rao: Hi, Priya from Redwood, I'm the solutions engineer, I'll own the technical side of the POC.
[00:29] Samir Gupta: Samir, customer success, will help with onboarding and timelines.
[00:33] Jordan Kim: Great. High level — objective today is to align on security/compliance checklist for the pilot and nail down success criteria, sizing, and benchmarks.
[00:43] Lena Morales: Our goal is to validate that Redwood can meet our security posture and performance targets before we expand. Specifically, we need SOC 2 Type II or equivalent, ISO attestations, SSO via our IdP (SAML), RBAC, and immutable audit logs. Also want to understand options for private deployment in our VPC or on-prem.
[01:00] Jordan Kim: Totally. We can cover each of those. Quick question on SOC 2 — do you require Redwood to be in-scope right away, or is acceptable to rely on our attestation and shared responsibility model for the pilot?
[01:12] Dr. Aaron Patel: For a pilot with customer data, we require proof of SOC 2 Type II and the ability to demonstrate controls; we also need to know retention and encryption practices. For production we'd look for tighter controls but for pilot we need the attestation and SOC 2 report.
[01:26] Priya Rao: Understood. We'll share the SOC 2 report and our ISO 27001 summary. For encryption we use TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest; we can integrate with customer KMS or HSM in private deployments.
[01:41] Ethan Brooks: If you integrate with our KMS, do you support AWS KMS and GCP KMS, and what about dedicated HSM?
[01:48] Priya Rao: Yes, we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS integrations; HSM via customer-managed nodes in the private deployment, we can discuss details in the architecture review.
[01:57] Marcus Lee: On RBAC — we need role separation: sequestered admin, ops, and read-only auditing roles. Can Redwood map to our IdP groups?
[02:07] Jordan Kim: Yes, Redwood's RBAC integrates with SAML assertions and SCIM for provisioning. You can map IdP groups to our roles; we also have a fine-grained permission set for token scoping.
[02:18] Zoe Han: Audit logs — do you provide immutable logs with export and retention controls? We need to retain for 7 years for certain data types.
[02:27] Priya Rao: We provide append-only audit logs and can export to your SIEM — Splunk/Datadog — and we support configurable retention for private deployments. For hosted accounts there's a standard retention but enterprise plans can extend retention.
[02:40] Dr. Aaron Patel: Good. What about data residency? Pilot must keep data in our region (us-east-1) and be able to show where logs and tokens are stored.
[02:50] Jordan Kim: We can pin the pilot to a specific region and either host in our dedicated capacity in that region or use the private VPC deployment. We'll document where artifacts live.
[02:59] Lena Morales: Moving to success criteria — what do you propose?
[03:02] Priya Rao: For this type of pilot we usually define: functional correctness (quality of responses on our test prompts), performance (p95 latency under X ms — what's your target?), throughput (tokens/sec and concurrent requests), and security/compliance validation.
[03:18] Marcus Lee: For latency we'd like p95 under 300ms for typical interactive prompts, and throughput to sustain our peak of about 120 qps with an average of 600 tokens per request during business hours.
[03:30] Priya Rao: OK 120 qps with 600 tokens avg — that maps to ~72k tokens/sec peak. We'll size for a buffer. For benchmarking we'll need representative prompts and a replay of traffic for a 2-day run.
[03:44] Marcus Lee: We'll provide representative prompt set and a replay capture by end of week.
[03:48] Jordan Kim: On measurement — we'll instrument latency at the client-side and server-side. Priya will define the benchmark harness (load generator, sequence lengths, KV cache warm/cold runs).
[03:59] Priya Rao: Benchmark plan: warm-up, 24-hour stability run, 2-day burst run with peak windows, and error-rate tracking. We'll capture tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens estimate, and memory/GPU utilization.
[04:12] Dr. Aaron Patel: For benchmarks, we also want to run a security test: try to exfiltrate PII from model outputs and test prompt-injection hardening.
[04:20] Priya Rao: Absolutely — we'll include tests for prompt injection, red-teaming prompts, and data leakage checks. We'll provide an eval harness and suggested test cases.
[04:28] Lena Morales: How long is a realistic pilot?
[04:31] Samir Gupta: Typical POC is 4 to 8 weeks: week 0 provisioning and onboarding, weeks 1-2 integration and baseline benchmarks, week 3 full performance runs and security scans, week 4 wrap and go/no-go decision. If you want on-prem or private deployment it can extend by 2 weeks for infra installs and KMS setup.
[04:50] Marcus Lee: So 6 weeks expected if we go with VPC + KMS?
[04:53] Samir Gupta: Yes that's reasonable.
[04:55] Jordan Kim: Regarding SSO — we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user sync. For the pilot we can do SAML SSO and manual mapping, then SCIM to automate provisioning in production.
[05:06] Ethan Brooks: Do you support IdP-initiated flows and SP-initiated?
[05:09] Priya Rao: Both. We'll send the SSO integration guide.
[05:12] Zoe Han: Are auth logs forwarded to our SIEM in real time?
[05:16] Priya Rao: Yes, we can stream audit events to your SIEM via secure webhook or syslog connector in private setups.
[05:23] Dr. Aaron Patel: For compliance we need a runbook of incident response and how you handle subpoenas and data requests.
[05:30] Jordan Kim: We'll include our IR runbook summary in the security pack. We also have SOC 2 controls mapping to NIST and can show how evidence is collected.
[05:40] Marcus Lee: Back to workload sizing — can you give a ballpark of GPU footprint for our profile? 120 qps, 600 tokens avg, p95 300ms?
[05:51] Priya Rao: Ballpark: depends on model family and quantization. For a 70B quantized model on A100s, expect X GPUs for sustained 120 qps — rough estimate 4-6 GPUs with batching and KV cache; we'll finalize after reviewing sequence length distribution. If you want lower cost we can use a 13B optimized model — tradeoff is quality vs cost.
[06:15] Marcus Lee: We'll include model preference in the doc; we prefer an open model that matches our quality bar.
[06:19] Jordan Kim: We'll run model comparisons during the pilot; Priya will recommend quantization profiles and kernels.
[06:24] Lena Morales: For data handling — do you ingest or persist raw prompts? We need to ensure PHI is not stored.
[06:31] Priya Rao: For hosted, we have configurable retention and can disable retention for certain routes. For private deployments, you control all storage. During the pilot we can configure no-persist on dev routes and demonstrate logs routing to your SIEM.
[06:44] Dr. Aaron Patel: Encryption keys — we need to see key rotation policies and ability to use our KMS so you don't hold plaintext keys.
[06:51] Priya Rao: We'll share KMS integration docs and our key rotation schedule; for private deployments keys never leave your account.
[06:58] Jordan Kim: Quick note on pricing for the pilot — we'll give a time-limited pilot credit for the benchmarking window, and then provide a proposal for Dedicated capacity if you move to production.
[07:07] Lena Morales: Good. Competitor callouts — we evaluated DatumAI and CloudEndpoints; main differences are latency predictability and support for private deployments. Your ability to run in our VPC is important.
[07:20] Jordan Kim: Understood. We'll highlight architecture differences in the materials we send.
[07:24] Marcus Lee: On the benchmarks — what tooling will you use for load generation?
[07:28] Priya Rao: We use a harness built on Locust and a custom token-aware driver that replays variable sequence lengths and can simulate KV cache warm/cold. We'll provide the harness as a container you can run in your environment.
[07:40] Ethan Brooks: If we run the benchmark in our VPC, will Redwood need access to our network?
[07:45] Priya Rao: For private deployment, we'll run the runtime inside your VPC; Redwood's control plane can be configured to be customer-managed. We'll walk through network requirements in the architecture review.
[07:56] Lena Morales: Let's capture explicit success criteria now for the pilot: 1) p95 latency <= 300ms on representative interactive prompts, 2) sustained throughput of 120 qps with error rate < 0.5%, 3) RBAC + SAML SSO working end-to-end, 4) Audit logs exported to our SIEM and retention configured, 5) SOC 2/ISO docs provided and reviewed. Is that right?
[08:19] Jordan Kim: Yes, that's a solid set. We'll add: 6) No unacceptable data exposures in the red-team tests and prompt-injection tests.
[08:29] Dr. Aaron Patel: Agree. Also require evidence of KMS integration or documentation if not done in pilot.
[08:35] Priya Rao: We'll add KMS integration as a checklist item.
[08:38] Marcus Lee: Timeline recap?
[08:40] Samir Gupta: Proposed timeline: Day 0 provisioning and SSO setup, week 1 integration and small scale tests, week 2 baseline benchmarks, week 3 full perf and security runs, week 4 wrap. If VPC/on-prem involved add two weeks for infra and KMS. So total 4-6 weeks.
[08:58] Lena Morales: Sounds good. We'll aim to start provisioning next week.
[09:02] Jordan Kim: Action items I'll summarize in an email. We'll attach the security pack (SOC 2/ISO, penetration testing summary), the SSO guide, and the benchmark plan.
[09:11] Priya Rao: I'll follow up with the benchmark spreadsheet — will include workload knobs (batch size, concurrency, model variant) and expected GPU footprint estimates.
[09:19] Marcus Lee: We'll provide sample prompts and traffic capture by Friday.
[09:23] Zoe Han: I'll review the privacy section and confirm any required DPA clauses.
[09:27] Dr. Aaron Patel: We'll want to schedule the architecture review with our infra team — send possible slots for week of May 28th.
[09:35] Jordan Kim: Noted. Any other questions?
[09:36] Marcus Lee: One question on logging format — is audit log schema documented? We need timestamps, user id, session id, request/response hashes, and admin actions.
[09:46] Priya Rao: Yes, we'll include the audit log schema in the pack; it contains structured JSON events with those fields and optional PII redaction hooks.
[09:55] Ethan Brooks: For the on-prem installer, is Helm chart available?
[09:59] Priya Rao: For private deployments we have a Helm chart + IaC templates and an installer runbook. We'll share them in the repo access.
[10:07] Lena Morales: OK great. 
[10:09] Jordan Kim: Recap of next steps: Redwood -> security pack, SSO guide, benchmark plan. Bayfront -> traffic profile, prompt set, infra stakeholders. Schedule arch review. We'll follow up with a meeting invite.
[10:22] Samir Gupta: I'll coordinate and send invites. Thanks everyone.
[10:26] Meeting end.
